- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model lags in catching the shift; forecast should rise 1–2% faster than historical trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by > 2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.
